Individual-level dietary diversity indicators follow the same principle as the HDDS described above. The most common indica-
tors used are the Minimum Dietary Diversity for Women of reproductive age (MDD-W) and the Minimum Dietary Diversity (MDD)
for children. In many contexts, women’s nutrition knowledge is central for household food security and nutrition as their child’s
diet quality tends to be closely linked to their own (Bonis-Profumo et al., 2020; Debela et al., 2017). Both indicators have been
